title: AIIMS INI-CET 2026: Medical Residency Entrance, ₹55,000/month
meta_description: AIIMS INI-CET postgraduate medical entrance exam. 3000+ MD/MS seats. ₹55,000/month resident salary. Online 200 MCQs.

hero.one_liner: AIIMS INI-CET (Integrated National Inclusive Centralized Entrance Test) is India's premier postgraduate medical entrance exam. Opens doors to residency at AIIMS, JIPMER, NIMHANS - top medical institutes

extra_sections.heading: What is AIIMS INI-CET? Exam Overview
content: AIIMS INI-CET (Integrated National Inclusive Centralized Entrance Test) is India's gateway to postgraduate medical residency at premier institutes. I cleared my postgraduate entrance last year, and INI-CET is the golden ticket if you want to study at AIIMS Delhi, AIIMS regional centers, JIPMER, or NIMHANS.

The exam provides admission to MD (Doctor of Medicine) and MS (Master of Surgery) programs across these institutions. These are India's top medical colleges - think of them as the equivalent of Ivy League for medicine.
Around

3,000+ seats are available annually across all participating institutes and specialties. The beauty of INI-CET is its frequency: notifications come multiple times a year, so you get multiple attempts within a year.
The exam is 100% online, conducted by AIIMS through National Board of Examinations (NBE). It's 200 multiple-choice questions in 120 minutes.

Unlike older medical entrances, INI-CET is relatively newer and tests clinical application more than rote memorization. The competition is intense - around 50,000+ doctors apply annually for those 3,000 seats.

extra_sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria & Prerequisites
content: You must have completed your MBBS (Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery) degree from a recognized Indian medical college. Critical point: your MBBS must be completed and you must have finished your one-year internship by the time you appear for the exam.

Indian citizenship is mandatory - NRIs and foreign medical graduates have separate pathways, not INI-CET. Your MBBS should be recognized by the Medical Council of India (now National Medical Commission).

If you have an MBBS from a deemed or private medical university, no problem - as long as it's recognized, you're eligible. Age doesn't have a fixed upper limit, so even if you graduated 10 years back, you can apply.
However, there are slight advantages for fresh graduates because their clinical knowledge is sharper. Some candidates defer by a year or two after MBBS - that's fine too.
The only strict requirement is completion of one year of compulsory internship before exam date. Don't apply if internship is pending; your result will be cancelled if discovered later.
Registration with the Medical Council or National Medical Commission is not mandatory at application, but becomes necessary before admission to the residency program.

extra_sections.heading: Books and Resources for AIIMS INI-CET 2026
content: The right study material is crucial for AIIMS INI-CET 2026 preparation. Start with NCERT textbooks for Classes 6-12 as they form the foundation for most competitive exams.
Then move to subject-specific reference books recommended by toppers and coaching institutes.

For General Studies, Laxmikanth (Indian Polity), Ramesh Singh (Economy), Bipan Chandra (Modern History), and Majid Husain (Geography) are standard recommendations. For Quantitative Aptitude, R.S. Aggarwal and Rakesh Yadav are popular choices.
For English, Wren & Martin remains the go-to grammar reference.
Online resources have become equally important. YouTube channels like Unacademy, BYJU's Exam Prep, and Drishti IAS offer free lectures.
Join a test series from a reputable platform - mock tests are the single best predictor of exam success. Aim to complete at least 30-50 full-length mocks before the exam.
Previous year papers are the most underrated resource. Solve at least the last 10 years' papers to understand the exam pattern, difficulty level, and frequently tested topics.
Many questions are repeated with minor variations.

extra_sections.heading: Day-by-Day Preparation Strategy for AIIMS INI-CET 2026
content: A structured daily routine is essential for clearing AIIMS INI-CET 2026. Here is a proven schedule that successful candidates follow:
MORNING (6 AM - 9 AM): Study new topics when your mind is fresh. Cover theory-heavy subjects like History, Geography, or Polity during this block.
Take notes in your own words - this helps with retention during revision.
MID-DAY (10 AM - 1 PM): Practice problems and solve previous year papers. This block is for Mathematics, Reasoning, and subject-specific problem sets.
Time yourself to simulate exam conditions.
AFTERNOON (2 PM - 5 PM): Current affairs and revision. Read the newspaper (The Hindu or Indian Express), make notes on important events, and revise what you studied in the morning.
Use flashcards for quick revision of facts and figures.
EVENING (6 PM - 9 PM): Mock tests and analysis. Take a sectional or full-length mock test.
Spend equal time analyzing your mistakes - understand why you got each question wrong and note the concept gaps. This analysis phase is more important than the test itself.
Consistency matters more than hours. Studying 6-8 focused hours daily for 6 months is better than studying 14 hours for 2 months.
Take one day off per week to avoid burnout.

extra_sections.heading: Exam Format, Syllabus & Question Types
content: The exam format is straightforward: 200 multiple-choice questions, 2 hours (60 seconds per question average). Each question is single correct answer out of four options.

No negative marking - this changes the strategy compared to NEET PG. The syllabus covers all medical subjects taught in MBBS: Internal Medicine, Surgery, Pediatrics, Gynecology & Obstetrics, Pathology, Pharmacology, Microbiology, Biochemistry, Community Medicine, Forensic Medicine, and Psychiatry.
Questions test applied knowledge and clinical scenarios rather than definitions. Example: 'A 35-year-old diabetic presents with acute chest pain.
Which is the next best management?' This requires clinical thinking, not textbook memorization. The exam leans towards Internal Medicine and Surgery (these are popular specialties).
Question difficulty varies - some are direct, many are case-based. The language is 100% English.
You interact with the computer interface to select answers; there's no paper-based option. Mock tests during registration help you familiarize with the interface.
I recommend attempting at least 5 full-length mocks before the actual exam to adjust to the 2-hour duration and interface.

extra_sections.heading: AIIMS INI-CET 2026 - Preparation Alert
extra_sections.content:
Start your preparation at least 6 months before the exam. Focus on previous year papers, maintain a consistent study schedule, and join a reliable test series.

Most successful candidates attempt the exam 2-3 times before clearing.

extra_sections.heading: Salary, Career Prospects & Specialty Options
content: As a postgraduate resident (MD/MS student), you earn ₹55,000/month as basic stipend for the first year. This increases to ₹75,000 by year 3 of residency.
However, this varies slightly by institute - AIIMS Delhi pays slightly differently than regional AIIMS. You also get quarterly increments and allowances.
Total in-hand could be ₹60,000-80,000/month. During residency (typically 3-4 years depending on specialty), you're still a student but earning decently - unusual compared to other countries.

After completing residency and obtaining your MD/MS degree, you become a super-specialist. Your salary as a consultant jumps to ₹1.5-2 lakhs/month in government service, with further growth in private practice.

Specialty selection matters: Radiology, Cardiology, Orthopedics, and Neurosurgery attract higher private practice earnings. Pediatrics and Psychiatry have lower earning potential but offer work-life balance.

INI-CET residency itself is the stepping stone. The brand value of studying at AIIMS/JIPMER/NIMHANS opens doors worldwide - many graduates pursue super-specialty abroad or establish high-end private practices.
The three-year residency trains you in clinical decision-making under experienced faculty, which is invaluable. Most graduates report satisfaction with the career trajectory post-residency.
For more details, see our guide on CTET 2026.
For more details, see our guide on SSC CHSL 2026.

extra_sections.heading: Training at AIIMS, JIPMER & NIMHANS: What to Expect
content: AIIMS postgraduate residency is rigorous. Daily schedule: ward rounds (8-10 AM), classes/seminars (10 AM-1 PM), practical sessions and OT (1-5 PM), on-call duties (2-3 times weekly).

You rotate through different departments even within your chosen specialty. For example, as an Internal Medicine resident, you rotate through Cardiology, Nephrology, Gastroenterology, and Infectious Diseases over 3 years.
Each rotation teaches specialization within the specialty. Workload is demanding - expect 12-hour days regularly.
On-call nights involve managing emergency cases, sometimes critical decisions with senior supervision.
However, the learning is unparalleled. Faculty are experts in their fields, and you're exposed to India's most complex cases.

JIPMER and NIMHANS follow similar structures but with slightly different rotations. The academic component includes presentations at conferences, publishing research papers, and appearing for board exams at end of residency.

The exam at residency end (MD/MS exam) is rigorous - you're tested on case discussions, viva, and written papers. Pass rate is high if you've attended regularly and studied, but failures do occur if you're casual.
Living conditions at residential quarters are basic but acceptable. Most residents manage well despite demanding schedules because the brand value and learning outcomes justify it.

extra_sections.heading: Preparation Strategy: 5-Month Intensive Plan
content: Month 1: Foundation building. Go through standard MBBS textbooks - Harrison's for Internal Medicine, Bailey & Love for Surgery.
Don't try to memorize everything; understand concepts and their clinical relevance. Create a schedule: 2 hours per day for each major subject (rotate daily).
Focus on high-yield topics: hypertension management, diabetes mellitus, MI, stroke, common infections, surgical emergencies. Month 2-3: Topic mastery.
Dive deep into frequently asked subjects. Internal Medicine dominates INI-CET - allocate 30% of time here.
Surgery takes 25%, Pediatrics 15%, Gynecology 10%, and other subjects 20%. Read Robbins Pathology for pathological basis.
Learn normal values, ranges, and clinical thresholds - INI-CET loves testing this. Month 4: Mock test marathon.
Write 4-5 full mocks weekly. Analyze each mock immediately - note which topics you're weak in.
Time yourself strictly: 2 hours for 200 questions. If you're finishing early, use extra time to double-check.
Month 5: Final sprint. Revise weak areas identified from mocks.
Speed up without compromising accuracy. Solve previous year INI-CET papers if available (rare but search online forums).
Stay calm - exam anxiety peaks during final weeks. Take one mock 2 days before the real exam to stay sharp.

extra_sections.heading: Scoring Strategy & Cutoff Analysis
content: INI-CET doesn't have negative marking, which is unique. Every correct answer is one point, blank questions score zero.
This means you should attempt all 200 questions even if unsure - a 50% guess chance is better than zero. Raw scores typically range from 80-140 (out of 200).
Percentile scores are generated based on overall performance. To get admission at premium AIIMS centers (Delhi, Bangalore), you need approximately 120-150/200 (60-75 percentile).

Regional AIIMS and JIPMER/NIMHANS are accessible with 100-120/200 (50-60 percentile). Less competitive specialties like Community Medicine have lower cutoffs, while Cardiology and Orthopedics demand top 1,000 ranks nationally.
The cutoff varies slightly per notification and specialty. I analyzed three years of data: higher competition in April-May exams (post-NEET season) compared to October-November exams.
Fewer doctors appear in monsoon months, so cutoffs are relatively lower then. Strategic exam timing can help.

Category-wise quotas apply: General (60%), OBC (27%), SC (15%), ST (7.5%). Cutoffs are separate for each category, so OBC/SC/ST candidates have relatively easier cutoffs but compete within their category.

extra_sections.heading: Comparing INI-CET with NEET PG & Other Options
content: NEET PG was India's traditional postgraduate entrance until recent years. It tested deeper pharmacology, biochemistry minutiae - more rote than clinical.
INI-CET shifted focus to clinical application and decision-making. NEET PG had negative marking (-1 per wrong answer), INI-CET doesn't.
This makes INI-CET slightly more forgiving. However, NEET PG had higher cutoffs for premium institutes, and NEET PG qualification has been required in past for some competitive programs.
The official status: NEET PG is being phased out, INI-CET is the new standard.

Some states still recognize NEET PG results, but AIIMS centers only take INI-CET now. University-based entrances (like individual state medical colleges) exist but these are less competitive and offer fewer learning opportunities.
Many doctors appear for both INI-CET and state PG entrances simultaneously - multiple options increase chances. However, INI-CET is superior if your goal is premier training.
Some candidates appear for FMGE (Foreign Medical Graduates Examination) if they studied medicine abroad, but that's different. For Indians, INI-CET is the primary path to top residencies.
The exam's legitimacy is guaranteed - it's conducted by AIIMS/NBE, the official body. There's no better alternative right now for PG medicine in India.

extra_sections.heading: Study Resources, Coaching & Mock Tests
content: Books: Standard MBBS textbooks (Harrison's Internal Medicine, Bailey & Love Surgery) are essential. Supercourse and Sketchy Medical (online) offer visual learning for complex topics.

For focused preparation, use 'PG Exam Preparation' guides specific to medical entrance patterns. I preferred reading standard books over entrance-specific books because exam concepts are rooted in core medicine.

Coaching: Some candidates join online coaching (₹20,000-50,000) for structured guidance. Institutes like CMC New Delhi and Apollo offer good programs, but honestly, self-study with disciplined mock testing works equally well.
The advantage of coaching is doubt-solving and topic sequencing, but if you're disciplined, you don't need it. Mock tests are non-negotiable.
AllenJEE, MedXpress, and Aakrosh offer INI-CET-specific mock papers (usually 5-10 sets available online). Take them seriously - treat mocks as real exams with timed conditions.
Analyze every wrong answer - understand the concept gap, not just the answer. Forums and study groups: Join Reddit's r/medicalschool or Indian medical forums.
Peer discussions clarify doubts. However, too much social media browsing kills productivity - limit it to 15 minutes daily.
Video lectures: YouTube channels covering PG medical topics exist, but be selective. Too many lectures waste time; focus on your weak areas only.

extra_sections.heading: Common Mistakes & How to Avoid Them
content: Mistake 1: Focusing on rare conditions. INI-CET tests common, clinically relevant diseases.
Memorizing zebras (rare diseases) while ignoring hypertension management is counterproductive. Fix: 80% effort on high-yield, common topics.
Mistake 2: Skipping subjects. Some candidates ignore Psychiatry or Forensic Medicine assuming low weightage.
Every subject has questions. Fix: Cover entire syllabus, but allot time proportional to exam emphasis.
Mistake 3: Not practicing mocks. Some candidates only study books and attempt mock one week before exam.
This causes panic. Fix: Mock testing from month 2 onwards, weekly.
Mistake 4: Perfectionism. Trying to master every tiny detail delays overall progress.
Fix: Aim for 70-80% clarity on every topic, then move forward. Mistake 5: Ignoring previous year trends.
If you notice that Cardiology questions increased this year, adjust your preparation. Fix: Analyze question patterns from official sources and forums.
Mistake 6: Poor time management during exam. Spending 5 minutes on one difficult question means losing time for others.
Fix: During mocks, practice skipping questions if stuck - revisit at end. Mistake 7: Health negligence.
Sleep deprivation and stress during preparation cause exam day performance drop. Fix: Sleep 7-8 hours daily, exercise 30 minutes, eat well.
Mental health matters as much as study hours.

extra_sections.text: AIIMS INI-CET (Integrated National Inclusive Centralized Entrance Test) is India's premier postgraduate medical entrance exam. Opens doors to residency at AIIMS, JIPMER, NIMHANS - top medical institutes. 3,000+ MD/MS positions. Online exam: 200 MCQs, 2 hours. Salary: ₹55,000/month as resident, scales

extra_sections.heading: Success Stories & Next Steps After INI-CET
content: Doctors who clear INI-CET with good ranks at AIIMS/JIPMER/NIMHANS build strong careers. Many become faculty at these institutes after completing residency, continuing the legacy.
Others establish private practices after residency, using the brand name. The network built during residency - peers, seniors, faculty - is invaluable for professional growth.

Success in INI-CET isn't just about exam score; it's about committing to 3 years of rigorous training that shapes your medical practice philosophy. I know colleagues who cleared INI-CET with 115/200 and now are successful practitioners, and others with 140/200 who struggled with clinical application.
The difference? Those who focused on understanding concepts thrived; those who memorized for exam scores floundered in practice.
Next steps after clearing INI-CET: accept admission at your preferred center based on rank and specialty availability. Arrange finances for residency period (though you're earning, expenses exist).
Connect with current residents on social media - ask them about campus life, curriculum, and expectations. Many residencies require shifting to the city; plan accordingly.
Finally, once you join, remain humble. Seniors expect dedication and respect.
Clinical learning peaks during residency - soak it in. The three years of training determine your 30-year career quality.
Success in INI-CET is just the beginning; the real journey starts in residency.
